section: Educational Psychology · Ch6 — Intelligence — Deep Practice 3
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: A student who devises a novel, unconventional approach to solve an unusual problem no one has taught them is displaying strong:

options.option_text: Creative (experiential) intelligence, in Sternberg's triarchic model

explanation: Sternberg's creative/experiential intelligence involves dealing with novelty and generating original solutions — distinct from analytical (academic problem-solving) and practical (real-world application) intelligence.

section: Educational Psychology · Ch6 — Intelligence — Deep Practice 3
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: A child who excels at recognising and classifying plants, animals and natural patterns is showing strength in which of Gardner's later-added intelligence?
explanation: Gardner added naturalistic intelligence (recognising and classifying elements of the natural world) after his original seven intelligences — relevant to careers like biology, farming, and environmental science.
